title: How to Paint Kitchen Cabinets: A Pro's Step-by-Step Process
description: Professional cabinet painting means emptying and masking the kitchen, removing doors and hardware, degreasing, sanding, priming, filling and spraying cabinet enamel. Here's each step and why it matters.
author: Chris Petkau
content:
Short answer: professional cabinet painting follows the same order every time. Prep and seal off the room, remove doors, drawers and hardware, clean and degrease, scuff-sand and prime, fill and caulk, then spray a cabinet-grade enamel in thin, even coats. Finally, let the finish cure before reassembling. Skipping the degreasing or primer is the most common reason cabinet paint peels or chips.

Step 1: Prep and Seal Off the Room

Empty the cabinets, move tables and chairs out, and mask floors, countertops, backsplash, appliances and walls. Then wall off the kitchen with plastic so dust and spray stay contained.

Step 2: Remove Doors, Drawers and Hardware

Take off doors, drawer fronts, shelves, hinges and pulls. Label each door and its hinges so everything goes back where it came from. Doors and drawers are usually finished separately from the cabinet boxes.

Step 3: Clean and Degrease

Kitchen cabinets carry years of cooking grease and hand oils, and paint won't bond to grease. Every surface gets a thorough degreasing clean.

Step 4: Scuff-Sand and Prime

Lightly sand the existing finish, or use a deglosser, so the primer has something to grip. Then apply a bonding primer made for cabinets. Some painters skip primer to save time; it's the step that keeps the finish from chipping.

Step 5: Sand, Fill and Caulk

After priming, sand smooth with fine-grit sandpaper (around 220), wipe with a tack cloth, fill holes and dents, and caulk open seams on the boxes and face frames.

Step 6: Spray the Finish Coats

For a smooth, factory-style finish without brush or roller marks, we spray a cabinet-grade enamel with an airless sprayer and a fine-finish tip. Thin, even coats prevent drips and runs; usually two finish coats over primer.

Step 7: Cure, Reassemble and Clean Up

Doors and drawers go back on once they're dry enough to handle, with hardware reinstalled and adjusted. Cabinet enamel keeps hardening for weeks, so go easy on fresh doors at first. Wipe with a soft cloth, and don't scrub hard for the first few weeks.

Frequently Asked Questions

How long does professional cabinet painting take?

A typical kitchen takes several days to about a week, including prep, primer, coats and drying time between coats.

Can you paint cabinets with a brush and roller?

You can, but spraying gives a noticeably smoother, more factory-like finish. See spray vs. brush and roll.

Should I paint or replace my cabinets?

If the boxes are solid and you like the layout, painting costs a fraction of replacement. Read repaint or replace cabinets.
